title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

errors: No substantive mathematical error. The equivalence 'X' ≪ L ⇔ X' ≪ G' (given X' ≪ F) relies on L = F ∩ G being an intersection at the level of supports, which is exactly what the cartesian squares assert.
Notational inconsistency: in the line on compatibility, the condition should read X' ≍ Y' (primed Y); the page writes 'Y' without a prime and with an ambiguous negation stroke.
The arrows in the déploiement diagram are drawn as double-headed, which is odd for inclusions of posets. Presumably they are just a sketch of the inclusion maps.

ideas.what: Supports (Ombres) of a figure, its sub-figures, their intersection and induced refinements form a lattice of cartesian (intersection) squares; the same holds for the posets of strata (déploiements).
ideas.modern_name: face posets / entrance-exit posets of stratified spaces; restriction of stratifications to closed unions of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in stratified and tame topology (Whitney, Thom, Mather; o-minimal cell decomposition, van den Dries)
ideas.where_published: Only programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 (tame topology); the axiomatics itself is unpublished.

ideas.what: Local criterion: compatibility of refinements F', G' of compatible figures F, G is detected on the overlap L = F ∩ G (Axiom C / Proposition).
ideas.modern_name: gluing / descent-type locality condition for refinements of stratifications (common refinement over a union)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (common refinements of stratifications, triangulation theorems)

ideas.what: Axiom D: 'disposition' (∥, disjointness/no contact) of refinements is likewise detected on the overlap, imposed axiomatically because it is automatic only set-theoretically.
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial axiom for disjointness of strata in an abstract stratified poset

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 abstract axiomatics of tame 'figures' is essentially undocumented in the literature. It consists of strata posets 𝓜 with relations ≤, ≪, ≍, ∥, Ombre (support) and déploiement, and has numbered axioms (Ax pol, Ax C, Ax D) designed so that refinements glue locally. This page is one routine but characteristic step of it: overlap criteria for compatibility and disjointness of refinements.
missed.quote: chacun des trois carrés est cartésien. Itou pour les déploiements
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an unpublished attempt at a purely combinatorial foundation of tame topology. It could be compared with o-minimal structures, with exit-path / poset-stratified approaches (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) and with regular cell complexes. The content of this particular page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification step within an unpublished axiomatic program. The overlap criteria are elementary set-theoretically; the interest lies only in the (little-known) existence and shape of the axiomatics, not in any new result on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'A+D' should read 'Ax D' (Axiome D, renamed 'Critère'), parallel to 'Ax C' on the previous page; similarly 'At D_0', 'At pol' on the next page are 'Ax D_0', 'Ax pol'.
'on a X' ≭ Y' should be 'on a X' ≍ Y'' (compatibility of strata of F' and G').
In Ax D the hypothesis is most likely 'X ≍ Y' (as in Ax C), not 'X ≭ Y'; the mark in the image is ambiguous.
'X, Y, X', Y' ∈ M' should be '∈ 𝓜'.
'Omb G'' is written in the image with a C-like G (Omb G', Omb G'_L); the transcription is otherwise correct.
In the sentence 'telles que X' ≪ L, Y' ≪ L', the struck-out text is a first attempt 'X' ≪ G'; the final parenthetical reads '(ce qui signifie d'ailleurs : X' ≪ G, Y' ≪ F)'.
